description: The line plot compares the Macro-F1 scores of two models—MATTER (ours) and w/o material information—across varying numbers of tokens, with the x-axis labeled "Number of tokens" ranging from 0.6 to 1.5 on a linear scale, and the y-axis labeled "Macro-F1 Score (%)" ranging from 48 to 58. The pink line, representing MATTER (ours), begins at approximately 55% at 0.6 tokens, rises to a peak of 58% near 1.0 tokens, and then declines to about 50% by 1.4 tokens. The purple line, representing the model without material information, starts at 52.5% at 0.6 tokens, peaks at 56% near 0.7 tokens, and then remains relatively stable around 52–53% until approximately 1.2 tokens, after which it drops sharply to 48% at 1.5 tokens. Shaded regions around each line indicate variance, with noticeable overlap between the two conditions near 1.2 tokens. Overall, MATTER consistently achieves higher Macro-F1 scores across all token counts, though both models show a decline in performance at higher token counts.
caption_used: Comparison of Macro-F1 scores for MATTER and w/o material knowledge during tokenization training across different numbers of tokens. The pink line representing MATTER (ours) starts at approximately 55% Macro-F1 Score, peaks at 58% near x=1.0, and ends at 50% near x=1.3, showing a consistent decline after its peak. The purple line, representing w/o material information, begins at 52.5%, peaks at 56% near x=0.7, and then stabilizes around 50% for the remainder of the range. The shaded areas indicate variance, with significant overlap between the two conditions near x=1.2. The results suggest that MATTER consistently outperforms the alternative across all token counts, with a sharper decline in performance at higher token counts for both conditions.
